previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, vasculitis, POTS, and malabsorption was readmitted two days after discharge due to severe epigastric and right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting triggered by eating a small amount of food. She had persistent dry heaves and was unable to tolerate oral intake initially. Imaging showed no acute abdominal process, including no evidence of pancreatitis or obstruction. She was managed with IV pain control and anti-nausea medications, then gradually advanced to a regular diet. Methotrexate was administered after confirmation with her PCP, despite a skin biopsy not showing vasculitis. Constipation was addressed with a PR regimen and oral laxatives. Her anxiety and orthostatic hypotension were managed with continued home medications. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with adjusted doses of escitalopram and betaxolol, and plans for outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:

chronic pancreatitis,  presenting with abdominal pain, nausea, 
vomiting, with course c/b an episode of ?hemetemesis.

# abdominal pain NOS - pt was initially treated with a regimen 
of IV dilaudid, ativan, IVF, and bowel rest as per her usual 
regimen.  Records from her recent evaluation at ___, 
___ were reviewed.  There was no evidence of acute 
intra-abdominal pathology.  Given her extensive, and recent 
imaging, further imaging studies were deferred.  Her abdomen was 
soft, she reported +flatus, and ongoing bowel movements, making 
SBO unlikely. 
. 
based upon her report of unwitnessed hemetemesis on the morning 
of ___, she was started on IV PPI BID, T&S sent, and urgent 
GI consult obtained.  As below, her symptoms were felt most 
likely due to suspected ___ tear from recurrent nausea 
and vomiting.  
.
an interdisciplinary team meeting held ___ including nursing 
staff, social work, and her pancreatologist, Dr. ___.  
Dr. ___ not feel that her symptoms could be explained with 
a diagnosis of pancreatitis.  Alternate GI sources of her 
abdominal pain were discussed and felt unlikely.  Other than 
repeat TSH testing, consideration was given for laboratory 
evaluation for porphyria, lead levels, and FMF which were all 
felt to be extremely unlikely diagnoses.  after reviewing her 
extensive GI workup with Dr. ___ additional diagnostic 
evaluation from a GI standpoint was felt available/necessary to 
further workup her symptoms.  As such, it was not felt that a GI 
source could be attributed to her symptoms presently. 
.
given the patient's report of benefit with methotrexate and 
prednisone in the past, a rheumatologic origin was considered.  
rheumatology consultation obtained in ___ did not feel that 
evidence was available to clearly support a diagnosis of 
Sjogren's disease or vasculitis, and did not recommend 
continuation of methotrexate. 
. 
to again review the primary data, repeat rheumatology consult 
was obtained.  after direct communication with the patient's 
PCP/rheumatologist ___, to again 
review the primary data available at ___ as well as with her 
PCP as below, ___ rheumatologic etiology of her recurrent 
abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting was again considered 
unlikely.  
.
her diagnosis of Sjogren's was also felt uncertain, although it 
was felt again unlikely that even a true diagnosis of Sjogren's 
could explain her abdominal symptoms.  Nevertheless, to provide 
a definitive answer, a parotid gland biopsy was scheduled for 
___ with Dr. ___ to provide a definitive answer (pt 
will f/u with Dr. ___ in ___ ___ to f/u these 
results, and obtain ophthalmologic exam as needed to evaluate 
for ophthalmologic symptoms of Sjogren's).  Strong concern was 
raised regarding the possibility of secondary gain. 
.
this provider, and the rheumatology consult service, did speak 
with Dr. ___ determined that the patient has no

given concerns about patient coping, narcotic 
tolerance/dependence, and addiction,(fears which the patient 
also expressed), as well as concerns about secondary gain, case 
was again reviewed with psychiatry.

based upon these results, it was felt that her symptoms of 
abdominal pain could not be explained with a unifying GI or 
___ medical diagnosis.  this was explained to the 
patient and her mother. 
. 
given lack of available/useful further diagnostic workup as per 
GI and rheumatology, a treatment based model was suggested, 
focused upon more consistent care with her primary care 
physician, long term psychiatric follow-up, and involvement of a 
chronic pain management team (ie. ___, with a goal of 
creating a regimen and close follow-up plan to minimize future 
hospitalizations.  when hospitalization for pain control is 
required, pt would seek care through the above providers first, 
locally.  if unable to provide pain relief locally, or should 
new symptoms or organ systems become involved, tertiary care 
referal could certainly be considered.  
. 
After discussing the above, pt elected to be discharged.  She 
was tolerating liquids only at this time, but ambulated without 
difficulty, and was moving her bowels.  I explained my 
preference that she stay until she could demonstrate ___ hours 
of symptoms which did not require IV narcotics, and the ability 
to tolerate oral and liquid diet, however, she felt she would be 
most comfortable at home.  She understood that we had not been 
able to identify a medical origin for her pain, and could be at 
risk for recurrence.  She will call her PCP or the emergency 
department should her symptoms recur.  She was provided with a 
prescription for Emend as below.

that repeat EGD was not warranted.  Her symptoms were attributed 
to presumed ___ tear from retching.  HCT decline was 
further attributed to aggressive hydration (200cc/hr 
continuous), and possible iron deficiency/anemia chronic 
disease.

to address the issue of repeated retching contributing to 
___ tear, a trial of Emend was recommended by GI 
service.  Pt notes typically good relief from n/v with oral 
zofran, however, on occasion, this fails to work, prompting 
admission.  She was given a prescription for a supply of Emend 
to use as a rescue medication for occasions when zofran failed 
to provide relief.  she was also provided with another 
prescription for oral zofran.
